greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who was lifted up for our salvation, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you were lifted up on the wood of the Cross to draw all people to yourself, Lord have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you emptied yourself to share in our humanity, Christ have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the source of eternal life for all who believe, Lord have mercy.
psalm_response: Do not forget the works of the Lord!
homily:
We often think of the Cross as a destination—a place where a story ends in silence and shadow. We look at the wood, the nails, and the weight of it, and our human instinct is to turn our eyes away. It is too heavy. It is too raw. And yet, the Scriptures today invite us to do something entirely counterintuitive. They invite us to look. 

In the desert, the people of Israel were dying. They were bitten by serpents, their bodies failing, their patience exhausted by the long, dry road. They cried out to Moses, 'We have sinned.' And the Lord, in His mysterious mercy, did not simply take the serpents away. Instead, He commanded Moses to craft a bronze serpent and mount it on a pole. He told them, 'If any who have been bitten look at it, they will live.' 

Think about that for a moment. Why a serpent? Why look at the very thing that was causing their pain? Perhaps it was to remind them that God is present even in the midst of the bite. Perhaps it was to strip away their denial, to make them face their reality in the presence of His healing. When they looked at that bronze image, they were not looking at the poison; they were looking at the sign of their salvation. They were looking at the command of God. 

Jesus takes this ancient image and places it squarely over His own life. 'Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert, so must the Son of Man be lifted up.' The Cross is no longer a symbol of defeat. It is the pole upon which our Salvation is raised. It is the place where God so loved the world that He gave His only Son. 

I think of Benjamin Vo today. I think of the way he looked at the world. Ben was a boy who loved to look up. He loved the clouds. He loved the mechanics of flight, the way a Boeing 737 cuts through the air, the way humanity has found a way to rise above the earth. He was a boy of curiosity, a boy who spent his time in GitHub repositories and cloud infrastructure, always trying to understand the architecture of things, always trying to see how the pieces fit together. He was a boy who looked at the world with a wide, bright, expectant gaze. 

There is a profound connection between that curiosity and the faith we celebrate today. To believe is to look. When the world is heavy—when the silence in your home, Alan and Thao, feels like a desert—the temptation is to look down. To look at the floor, to look at the empty chair, to look at the 'why' that has no answer. And yet, the Cross calls us to look up. It calls us to look at the One who was lifted up, not to condemn the world, but to save it. 

I want to speak to you, Ryan, about your brother. You shared so many moments of looking up together—standing on granite rocks in the mountains, watching the sky, dreaming of the next adventure. That brotherly bond is a work of the Lord. It is a work that does not end because the horizon has shifted. Ben is now looking at the face of the One who was lifted up for him. He is in the light where there is no more desert, no more sting, no more distance. He is the same Ben—curious, gentle, smiling—only now he is seeing the true architecture of the universe, the very mind of God he so loved to explore in his own brilliant, young way. 

Alan and Thao, I know the weight of the last three months. I know that the 'desert' of your grief has been a long and winding road. You have felt the sting of the loss, and you have felt the urge to complain, to ask, 'Why?' You are not alone in that. The people of Israel asked the same thing. But notice that God did not strike them down for their questions. He provided a way for them to live. He gave them a sign of hope. 

When you feel that the weight is too much, do not try to carry it by looking only at the ground. Look at the Cross. Look at the sacrifice of love that defines your son’s life. You see, Benjamin’s life was a life of giving. Think of that moment, so simple and so beautiful, when he wanted to offer his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't break it open; he didn't boast; he didn't make a scene. He simply offered. That was his 'bronze serpent' moment—the moment he looked at the needs of another and chose to be a sign of healing. He gave what he had, even when it wasn't needed, because his heart was already tuned to the frequency of the Kingdom. 

That love is not a memory. It is a force. It is the same love that is working in the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, bringing life-sustaining water to those who have none. It is the same love that lives in the quiet prayers you whisper at 3 a.m. It is the same love that binds your family of four together, across the veil of heaven and earth. 

There is a peace that comes when we stop trying to fix the desert and start looking at the One who walks through it with us. You have been faithful. You have loved with a depth that is a testament to the Gospel. You have not missed anything. You are not to blame for the storms that hit the house. You have been the guardians of a beautiful, gentle soul, and you remain his family, now and forever. 

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is a small thing, but a real thing. The next time the grief feels like a bite—the next time the sting of his absence feels sharp and sudden—do not look away. Do not close your eyes. Instead, look up. Look at the Cross in your room, or the crucifix in your heart. Whisper the name 'Jesus,' and then whisper the name 'Benjamin.' Let those two names be the pole upon which you fix your gaze. Remind yourselves: He is safe. He is held. And because he is held by the One who was lifted up, you are held, too. 

There is no distance that the Cross cannot bridge. There is no desert that the love of God cannot cross. Keep looking. Keep trusting. Keep being the family that loves so well. You are not walking toward an end; you are walking toward a reunion. And he is waiting for you in the light. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the blessing of Almighty God, the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, descend upon you and remain with you always. Go in peace, trusting in the love that lifts us up.
petition_call: In our need, we turn to the Lord and say,
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, that he may rest forever in the radiant light of Christ, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, we pray to the Lord.
For all who grieve, that the Lord may console them, lift their heavy hearts, and give them the hope of the Resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
With their patience worn out by the journey,

the people complained against God and Moses,

"Why have you brought us up from Egypt to die in this desert,

where there is no food or water?

We are disgusted with this wretched food!"



In punishment the LORD sent among the people saraph serpents,

which bit the people so that many of them died.

Then the people came to Moses and said,

"We have sinned in complaining against the LORD and you.

Pray the LORD to take the serpents from us."

So Moses prayed for the people, and the LORD said to Moses,

"Make a saraph and mount it on a pole,

and if any who have been bitten look at it, they will live."

Moses accordingly made a bronze serpent and mounted it on a pole,

and whenever anyone who had been bitten by a serpent

looked at the bronze serpent, he lived.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (see 7b) Do not forget the works of the Lord!

Hearken, my people, to my teaching;

incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

I will open my mouth in a parable,

I will utter mysteries from of old.

R. Do not forget the works of the Lord!

While he slew them they sought him

and inquired after God again,

Remembering that God was their rock

and the Most High God, their redeemer.

R. Do not forget the works of the Lord!

But they flattered him with their mouths

and lied to him with their tongues,

Though their hearts were not steadfast toward him,

nor were they faithful to his covenant.

R. Do not forget the works of the Lord!

But he, being merciful, forgave their sin

and destroyed them not;

Often he turned back his anger

and let none of his wrath be roused.

R. Do not forget the works of the Lord!

readings.label: Reading 2
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:

Christ Jesus, though he was in the form of God,

did not regard equality with God something to be grasped.

Rather, he emptied himself,

taking the form of a slave,

coming in human likeness;

and found human in appearance,

he humbled himself,

becoming obedient to death,

even death on a cross.

Because of this, God greatly exalted him

and bestowed on him the name

that is above every name,

that at the name of Jesus

every knee should bend,

of those in heaven and on earth and under the earth,

and every tongue confess that

Jesus Christ is Lord,

to the glory of God the Father.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus said to Nicodemus:

"No one has gone up to heaven

except the one who has come down from heaven, the Son of Man.

And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert,

so must the Son of Man be lifted up,

so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life."



For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son,

so that everyone who believes in him might not perish

but might have eternal life.

For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world,

but that the world might be saved through him.

day: Feast of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - need a miracle here. We miss you so much and we’re not sleeping much. Ryan wish you were here, especially this upcoming Saturday to play the new version of Project Flight with him.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Dear Ben, our uncle Thanh has passed away. Please watch over him and pray that his soul finds peace. His saint name is Phêrô. Lord, thank you for sending Chu Thanh into my life. I'll always be grateful for the time he spent tutoring me in math back in high school
